scale.meaning: 0 = does not satisfy the criterion at all; 5 = fully satisfies the criterion.

metrics.name: Relevance
metrics.question: Does the article remain consistently focused on the requested topic?
metrics.definition: Whether the document remains consistently aligned with the input topic and avoids irrelevant or generic digressions.

metrics.name: Breadth
metrics.question: Does the article provide broad coverage of the topic?
metrics.definition: Whether it covers the major background, principles, components, applications, challenges, evaluation aspects, and implications expected for the topic.

metrics.name: Depth
metrics.question: How thoroughly does the article explore the topic and its related areas?
metrics.definition: Whether it explains mechanisms, implementation details, module relationships, trade-offs, limitations, and technical implications beyond surface-level description.

metrics.name: Novelty
metrics.question: Does the article cover novel aspects that relate to the intent but are not directly derived from it?
metrics.definition: Whether it provides useful additional perspectives, comparisons, challenges, trends, or future directions beyond directly restating the topic.

metrics.name: Technical Specificity
metrics.definition: Whether core principles, system architecture, components, workflows, advantages, limitations, and deployment considerations are discussed with professional technical detail.

metrics.name: Understandability
metrics.definition: Whether the document is clear, coherent, readable, and uses technical terminology accurately and consistently.

metrics.name: Structurality
metrics.definition: Whether the section hierarchy, content order, section functions, transitions, and overall organization conform to technical-white-paper conventions.

metrics.name: Citation Sufficiency
metrics.definition: Whether key technical concepts, mechanisms, data, conclusions, and application claims receive adequate citation support across the document.

metrics.name: Citation Validity
metrics.definition: Whether citation identifiers can be matched to accessible references and whether each cited source directly supports its associated claim.

metrics.name: Factual Consistency
metrics.definition: Whether technical concepts, entities, relationships, mechanisms, and numerical statements agree with the retrieved evidence without contradiction or unsupported additions.

protocol.call_grouping: One call per metric group; each call receives the definitions of its own metrics together with the group-specific 0-5 rubric.
protocol.scores_per_call: One independent score per metric; no group-level aggregate score is requested from the evaluator.
protocol.aggregation: Arithmetic mean of the three independent runs for every metric.
protocol.randomization: Generated documents are randomly reordered before scoring.
protocol.reasoning: Enabled for Qwen3-32B; identical evaluator settings are used for all methods.

scoring_prompt.system: You are a strict and fair evaluator.
scoring_prompt.user_template:
[{instruction}]

Response:
[{response}]

Rubric:
{rubric}

Provide your evaluation in the following format:
[RESULT] Score: <score from 0 to 5>
<your detailed feedback>

overall_score: Unweighted mean of the ten metric scores.

residual_clustering.purpose: Module-level check that the multidimensional representation preserves category-discriminative structure.
residual_clustering.visualization: t-SNE projection used as a qualitative diagnostic only.

evaluators.profile: Graduate students with prior experience in technical white-paper writing.
evaluators.independence: Both evaluators independently review every document before any discussion.

labels.label: Directly Acceptable
labels.meaning: The document can be used without substantive revision.

labels.label: Acceptable with Minor Revisions
labels.meaning: The document is generally usable but requires localized corrections, supplementary explanations, or minor structural adjustments.

labels.label: Unacceptable
labels.meaning: The document has major deficiencies in technical content, organization, readability, or evidence support and requires substantial rewriting.

human_evaluation.disagreement_handling: When the initial labels differ, both evaluators independently re-examine the document against the predefined criteria and then discuss the reasons for their judgments until a consensus label is reached.

automatic_vs_human.automatic: Ten 0-5 metrics scored by an LLM evaluator over the three metric groups; reported as the mean of three runs.
automatic_vs_human.human: A three-level acceptability label per document, reached by consensus between two evaluators.
